name: SFIA: Sports and Fitness Industry Association landing page
title: SFIA: Sports and Fitness Industry Association landing page
answer: This is the Sports and Fitness Industry Association landing page, a promotional hub for SFIA research, advocacy and industry insights. Its most useful concrete item is that SFIA has released all 92 Single Sport Reports for 2026, covering total and CORE participation trends over five years and breakdowns by gender, age, education, region, income and ethnicity, plus cross-participation data for 2025. It also announces the 2026 Trends in Team Sports Report, Part I of II, and the 2034WARD campaign. It does not discuss AI.

sections.body: The Sports and Fitness Industry Association publishes this page. It is a landing page for SFIA, described as promoting sports and fitness participation through research, advocacy and industry insights. It promotes annual research reports, member access and the 2034WARD campaign. It refers to 2026 reports but does not state a publication date. Its scope is participation research and industry promotion, not a detailed article or dataset.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page states that SFIA promotes sports and fitness participation through research, advocacy and industry insights, driving growth across the sports and fitness industry. It announces the 2026 Trends in Team Sports Report: Participation Foundational Data, Part I of II in the Trends in Team Sports Reports Series, calling it a must-have report for anyone looking to understand team sports and the specific trends shaping the industry. It also describes the 2034WARD campaign, which it says will harness the global spotlight on sports and fitness to drive industry growth and participation. The page says the next decade will not wait and invites contact to learn how contributions and involvement will help SFIA expand sports and fitness participation 2034WARD. It offers access to annual research reports and exclusive member-only perks and asks readers to join. It states that SFIA has released all 92 Single Sport Reports for 2026. Those reports provide total and CORE participation trends over the last five years, breakdowns of participation by gender, age group, education, geographic region, income level and ethnicity, and a list of cross-participation data with other activities for 2025. The page does not give findings from those reports, only descriptions and promotional calls to action.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that SFIA has released all 92 Single Sport Reports for 2026. It says those reports cover total and CORE participation trends over the last five years and include breakdowns by gender, age group, education, geographic region, income level and ethnicity, plus cross-participation data with other activities for 2025. It names the 2026 Trends in Team Sports Report: Participation Foundational Data as Part I of II in the Trends in Team Sports Reports Series. It also names the 2034WARD campaign. It gives no AI figures or definitions.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in sports would find this source useful only as a pointer to participation data that could form market context for AI products, such as fan engagement, talent identification or participation analytics. The page itself contains no AI content, no technology adoption data and no youth or scholastic sports detail. It shows that SFIA is a publisher of participation reports and that its 2026 Single Sport Reports include demographic and cross-participation breakdowns. Anyone seeking AI-specific evidence would need to look beyond this landing page.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Sports

sections.body: This is a promotional landing page, not a research report or article. It does not provide the actual findings, methodology, sample sizes or definitions behind the reports it names. It does not mention artificial intelligence, technology adoption, equipment markets, youth sports or scholastic sports. It is commercial in tone, inviting membership, contact and contributions. It refers to 2026 reports and a 2034WARD campaign but states no publication date. The text is partial, consisting of promotional summaries and calls to action rather than substantive data.
